supported_summary: TRACE is a public computational method that uses inferred ancestral recombination graph features from present-day genomes. The authors report recovery of known archaic signals and infer a ghost contribution shared across sampled African and non-African populations plus a deeper contribution associated with Denisovan ancestry in Oceanians.
evidence_ceiling: The current package supports model-based ancestry-source hypotheses and genomic segment candidates. It does not support direct observation, named-species assignment, universal individual-level segment identity, adaptive causality, or independent replication by Kairos.
permitted_language: TRACE detected genomic signals consistent with introgression from previously uncharacterized archaic lineages.
The authors infer that ghost ancestry entered ancestors of sampled modern humans before the major Out-of-Africa expansion.
The authors infer a deeper contribution associated with Denisovan ancestry in Oceanian genomes.
The source populations remain taxonomically unidentified.
Functional enrichment is suggestive and does not establish adaptive causality.
forbidden_language: Scientists found DNA or fossils from two previously unknown human species.
Every person has the same ghost DNA.
The super-archaic ancestor was definitely Homo erectus.
The archaic fragments made humans immune or metabolically superior.
TRACE proves the unique demographic history without alternative explanations.
The study authorizes ancestry identity conclusions, experiments, or clinical action.
